tasks.brief: Build a playable two-scene signal-hunt Godot microgame implementing the frozen harbor/lighthouse API and all ten acceptance requirements. The goal is restoring the lighthouse signal.

rules: left/right/up/down move one cell within the 0..2 grid; successful state-changing actions increment state_version exactly once.
interact at harbor (1,0) acquires one gate_token if absent; never duplicate the item.
interact at harbor (2,0) without gate_token denies without changing canonical projection; the denial remains in trace.
interact at harbor (2,0) with gate_token opens gate, consumes the token once, and increments state_version once.
transition only at harbor gate (2,0) after gate_open; load the distinct lighthouse PackedScene resource and reset player to (0,0). Otherwise deny unchanged.
interact at lighthouse (1,1) sets restored and goal_complete; repeated completion does not duplicate a canonical effect.

repair immediately after the missing-token gate denial records the original interact candidate, error, a bounded corrected candidate left, its validation and commit; applies left to return to (1,0). It cannot fabricate a token/open the gate.

replay verifies/reconstructs prior accepted inputs without mutating current canonical projection; independent checker also resets a fresh instance and reapplies its own captured input sequence before comparing the final projection.
snapshot/observer/save are read-only and return detached data; load rejects malformed/out-of-domain data without mutation, and a valid save/load round trip preserves canonical state.
Trace records observed proposal, validation/denial, repair where attempted and state effect, not a hidden-state claim. Trace append alone does not increment state_version.

Both declared scene resources must load/instantiate. The active scene child is named Level with node name Harbor or Lighthouse under it, matching snapshot.scene; mere snapshot string changes without actual scene transition fail.

The built game is playable using arrow/WASD movement, E interact, T transition and R repair, with visible player, scene/goal information and denial feedback; headless checker does not establish human UX or physical input acceptance.

acceptance_suite.requirement: At least two named scenes load from a clean checkout and transition through the declared route without hidden manual setup.
Declared player movement/input works deterministically under the allowed input fixture and does not mutate frozen evidence.
The declared goal has a reproducible success condition and a visible/readable completion receipt.
The declared ontology/policy gate denies an unauthorized action and allows the authorized action using the frozen rule identifiers.
A bounded repair attempt records the original candidate, error, change and rerun; failed repairs remain traceable and do not silently commit.
A clean replay from the same receipt reproduces the declared decision, acceptance status and relevant state/hash outputs.
Observer/dashboard signals expose declared versus observed state and missing/unreported evidence without mutating game state or frozen inputs.
Save/load preserves the declared canonical state, version/hash and goal-relevant facts, with a receipt proving the round trip.
The approved existing build path, or a separately approved new runner, produces a runnable artifact from a clean checkout; unknown runner paths are not claimed as working.
Repeated deterministic QA on isolated copies produces the same declared outcomes and detects seeded valid corruptions without accepting false clean results.
